description:
FILED s473f (Opus, 2026-09-09), by a #1309 probe.  PRE-EXISTING.

    sub id { my $v = shift; return defined $v ? "[$v]" : "undef" }
    open(my $c, "<", "/etc/hostname") or die;
    printf "c=%s\n", id(scalar readline($c));
    printf "h=%s\n", id(scalar glob("/etc/hostname"));

    perl : c=[bernpad]        h=[/etc/hostname]
    PCL  : c=[1]              h=[1]

The value is the COUNT of the list the builtin produced in list context.

CAUSE, located: `%WANTARRAY_SENSITIVE` in Pl/ExprToCL.pm:203 lists
`reverse localtime gmtime caller unpack each splice readdir getprotobyname
getprotobynumber readpipe stat lstat` -- and NOT `readline` or `glob`.  So
`scalar FUNC(...)` in a list-context slot emits `(p-scalar (p-readline ...))`
INSIDE a `(p-list-ctx ...)`, i.e. the call runs in list context and `p-scalar`
then takes the LENGTH of the vector.

`scalar <$fh>` (the ANGLE spelling) is RIGHT -- a different node type, which is
why the bug is invisible in the common idiom.  `my $x = scalar readline($fh)`
is also right (the assignment imposes scalar context first); only an argument
slot / a print list is wrong.

The fix is presumably two words in that table, but it is EMISSION-CHANGING
(corpus-diff + a full sweep), which is why s473f filed it rather than riding it
in on a runtime-only batch.

Probes: scratch/s473f/p1i-scalarctx.pl, scratch/s473f/p1h-scalararg.pl.
subject: SILENT WRONG: `scalar readline($fh)` and `scalar glob($p)` in a LIST-context slot return the COUNT, not the value
